gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold: breathlessness for 2–3 days. Gen cc-001: shortness of breath and wheezing for 2–3 days. Shortness of breath ≈ breathlessness; timeframe matches. Added wheezing but does not negate breathlessness.
Gold: breathlessness for 2–3 days. Gen hpi-001: SOB and chest tightness began 2–3 days ago. Onset and duration of SOB match; chest tightness is additional.

Gold: SOB while running. No generated fact explicitly states SOB specifically while running; closest is hpi-001 (onset during running) but that addresses onset context, not that SOB occurs with running as a current trigger per se.

Gold: needing to use blue inhaler twice a day. Gen hpi-005: using blue salbutamol inhaler as needed and morning and evening to prevent symptoms, with lack of relief. This implies at least twice daily use (morning and evening).

Gold: normally uses blue inhaler only as needed. Gen hpi-005: using blue inhaler as needed and also in the morning and evening to prevent symptoms. The ‘as needed’ baseline is captured; added detail about additional prophylactic use now.
Gold: Clenil every day, 2 puffs twice daily. Gen hpi-006: preventer brown Clenil inhaler used twice daily. Frequency matches; dose ‘2 puffs’ omitted but not contradicted.
Gold: cough without sputum. Gen hpi-004: wheezing and coughing without sputum production. Matches and adds wheezing.
Gold: some wheezing. Gen hpi-004 and ros-001 both explicitly include wheezing. Symptom presence is captured.
Gold: asthma since childhood. No generated fact mentions onset in childhood; only current asthma diagnosis/exacerbation.
Gold: suffers from eczema. Gen pmh-002 mentions only ‘possible eczema (not confirmed)’, which weakens certainty and is not equivalent to a confirmed ongoing condition.
Gold: last asthma attack 3 years ago. Gen hpi-007: last asthma attack was 3–4 years ago; asm-003: last exacerbation over 3 years ago. Timeframe is consistent and inclusive of 3 years.

Gold: never needed antibiotics or steroids for asthma. Gen hpi-008: no prior hospital admissions or oral steroid use for asthma. Steroid component is covered; antibiotics not addressed but not contradicted.
Gold: never hospitalized because of asthma. Gen hpi-008: no hospital admissions reported. This matches.
Gold: normal peak flow 380 L/min. Gen hpi-011 and pe-003: usual/normal peak flow ~380 L/min. Matches.
Gold: has not had asthma check in last 2 years. Gen hpi-009 and asm-003: last asthma review approximately 2 years ago. This implies no review in the last 2 years and is consistent.
Gold: has hayfever. Gen allergy-001: hay fever listed. Matches.

Gold: Clenil 2 puffs twice daily. Gen hpi-006 and med-002: Clenil used twice daily; plan/med mentions suggested increase from 3 to 4 puffs, which is additional and slightly different than gold, but baseline ‘twice daily’ routine use is captured. Dose ‘2 puffs’ is omitted but not contradicted.

Gold: blue reliever currently up to twice daily. Gen hpi-005 and med-001: blue inhaler used as needed and in morning and evening. This reflects at least twice daily use; some extra prophylactic context but consistent.
Gold: uses hydrocortisone for eczema. Gen med-004: uses topical hydrocortisone (no indication stated). The medication use is captured; indication is implicit from gold only.
Gold: uses Cetraban for eczema. Gen med-003: uses Cetraben cream, likely for a skin condition. Medication is captured; indication is only inferred but not contradicted.
Gold: diagnosis mild asthma exacerbation. Gen asm-001: mild to moderate asthma exacerbation. Still includes ‘mild’; adds ‘moderate’ as an upper severity bound, but not opposite to mild exacerbation.
Gold: increase brown inhaler to 4 puffs twice daily. Gen plan-001 and med-002: increase Clenil to 4 puffs twice daily. Matches.
Gold: can use blue inhaler up to every 2–4 hrs. Gen plan-002: continue blue inhaler as needed up to every 2–4 hours. Matches; adds education about frequent use.

Gold: chest reviewed by a doctor within next 2 days. Gen plan-004/fu-001: book face-to-face GP appointment in ‘next few days’—timing is looser and does not clearly capture ‘within 2 days’ requirement.
Gold: if breathlessness worsens before seeing doctor, attend A&E. Gen plan-003: if breathing worsens significantly before appointment, go to emergency department. This is equivalent.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Shortness of breath for 2–3 days matches breathlessness for 2–3 days; wheezing is additional but consistent with gold wheeze in HPI.

Gold notes SOB while running but not the comparative functional statement ‘usually able to talk while running but recently became SOB.’ This nuance is new, not contradictory.

Coughing without sputum and wheezing are both in gold (hpi-006, hpi-007). Combined here but consistent.

Gold: no asthma check in last 2 years. Generated: last review ≈2 years ago. These are compatible ways of describing the review timing.

Family history (sister with eczema) is not mentioned in gold; entirely new.
